subject: Planned: East US3 maintenance window — hotpath curfew & rolling swap
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Acme Analytics Ops <acme-corp-ops@acme.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datafabrik.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: East US3 maintenance window — hotpath curfew & rolling swap

Hello —

We are scheduling a targeted maintenance window in the East US3 region on Friday, 2026-07-23 from 02:00 — 04:30 UTC. The work includes a low-risk kernel driver swap for select inference hosts and a brief hotpath curfew (prefix/KV cache thawing) to ensure consistency during the transition. Our goal is to avoid customer-visible interruption; however, brief <500ms tail-latency blips may occur on warm requests.

What to expect (summary):
- Window: 2026-07-23 02:00–04:30 UTC
- Scope: staged rolling swap of driver 5.2 -> 5.3 on 20% of warm host pools, followed by controlled roll forward
- Impact: 2–3 minute allocation rebalances per host, automated fallbacks to regional-compatible model variants if capacity constrained
- Safeguards: prefix KV cache warm-repopulation, automatic circuit-breaker thresholds, and immediate rollback playbooks if error rates rise >1.5% for 10 minutes

Attachments: kernel-patch-notes.pdf (summary + known issues), maintenance-matrix.csv (per-tenant impact matrix). We published the runbook and ticket at: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-9342 and shared the drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cExampleDriveLink

If you have a hard constraint (e.g., SLA-bound inference windows) and need exclusion from this specific wave, reply with your tenant identifier and we will place you on a no-touch list for this event.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Cloud Operations — Redwood Inference
log an@redwood.com

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned: East US3 maintenance window — hotpath curfew & rolling swap

Logan —

Thanks for the heads-up. Two quick operational notes for the announcement:
1) Please call out the exact fallback model variant names (we should reference redwood/compat-1 and redwood/compat-2) so customers know what will be used automatically.
2) Add short guidance about client-side reconnect/backoff recommendations for SDKs older than v0.9.2 — we've seen aggressive retries amplify the transient tail latency.

I've attached a trimmed maintenance-matrix.csv with tenant opt-outs already flagged from last quarter. Also, I'll own runway monitoring and will post to the status page (INF-9342) every 15 minutes during the window.

-Marcus
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
Attachments: maintenance-matrix.csv

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datafabrik.com>

Subject: Re: Planned: East US3 maintenance window — hotpath curfew & rolling swap

On Wed, Jul 21, 2026 at 10:05 AM Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com> wrote:
> We are scheduling a targeted maintenance window in the East US3 region on Friday, 2026-07-23 from 02:00 — 04:30 UTC.

Thanks for the advance notice, Logan. A couple questions from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the KV cache TTL will be preserved across the swap or whether we should expect cache misses for the first ~30k tokens served?
- For customers running long-running sessions (chat sessions pinned to a tenant), is there an opt-out mechanism to pin to a non-upgraded host pool during the window?

We can probably absorb small blips but want to plan for worst-case fallbacks.

— Sanjay
Lead Infrastructure Engineer — DataFabrik

-----
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datafabrik.com>, Acme Analytics Ops <acme-corp-ops@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned: East US3 maintenance window — hotpath curfew & rolling swap

Sanjay —

Good questions. Quick answers and mitigation plan: 
- KV cache behavior: The maintenance requires a brief prefix eviction during the host restart; caches will be repopulated automatically. Expected cache miss burst is targeted to the first ~5–10 requests per session (not token count) for affected hosts; we do not expect 30k-token miss storms. We are rate-limiting repopulation and honoring client-side request pacing to reduce thundering-herd.
- Opt-out/pinning: yes — send your tenant id and we will pin you to the no-upgrade pool for this wave. Note that pinned tenants will not receive the driver 5.3 perf improvements until a subsequent wave.

Operational notes: 
- If you see errors >0.5% for more than two consecutive 5-minute intervals, please open INF-9342 and tag @oncall. We'll execute the rollback playbook.
- Marcus will post check-ins on the status page every 15 minutes during the window.

I'll update the public note to include the fallback variant names and the SDK guidance that Marcus mentioned. If you want a short call Monday to walk through the runbook, happy to schedule — propose 09:00 UTC.

Thanks for raising this early; we'll make sure your tenancy is handled as requested.

— Logan
Head of Cloud Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: kernel-patch-notes.pdf (summary)
